segments.text: On the morning of September eighth, nineteen hundred, the telegraph line to Galveston went silent. A city of thirty-seven thousand people had woken to an ordinary sky.
In Havana, Father Gangoite had been watching the storm for days from the Belen Observatory. He believed it was turning toward Texas. His warnings did not reach the island.
Isaac Cline would later write that he had warned them. The records do not agree. By the time the water withdrew, eight thousand people were dead.
